aspects.says: A lambda captures a copy of a local's value; when the value is a reference, every copy points to the same heap object, which is then shared.
basis: section:Fields, Statics and Array Elements Are Shared; Locals and Parameters Are Not

aspects.says: @Contended is JDK-internal: it needs --add-exports to compile and is ignored in application classes unless the JVM runs with -XX:-RestrictContended.
basis: section:Threads That Share No Variable Can Still Share a Cache Line
aspects.reason: a practice can't set JVM flags or exports in the graded runner, and field offsets need sun.misc.Unsafe; the page shows both runs

aspects.says: Threads writing different variables in one cache line slow each other down; padding or @Contended separates the variables at a cost in memory.
basis: section:Threads That Share No Variable Can Still Share a Cache Line

aspects.says: InheritableThreadLocal copies values once, when a thread is created, so a pool's threads keep what their creator had; a value for a task is captured at submit time and set in the task.
basis: section:InheritableThreadLocal Copies the Value Once, When a Thread Is Created

aspects.says: Fields, statics and array elements are shared between threads while locals and parameters are not, so per-call state kept in a local is safe and the same state kept in a field of a shared object mixes overlapping calls.
basis: section:Fields, Statics and Array Elements Are Shared; Locals and Parameters Are Not

aspects.says: Caches are coherent; stale reads come from compiled code keeping a value in a register, from reordering and from store buffers, not from a per-thread copy of memory.
basis: section:Threads Don't Keep Private Copies of Memory; Compiled Code Keeps Values in Registers

aspects.says: A ThreadLocal value lives as long as its thread, so on a pool it must be removed in finally, or restored to the outer value when calls nest, or the next task on that thread sees it.
basis: section:A ThreadLocal Value Belongs to the Thread, So a Pool Hands It to the Next Task

aspects.says: A ThreadLocal value that is never removed keeps its memory as long as the pool's thread lives.
basis: section:A ThreadLocal Value Belongs to the Thread, So a Pool Hands It to the Next Task
aspects.reason: retained heap is measured after System.gc(), which a deterministic test cannot rely on; the tenant-context practice checks the removal that frees it
